headline: Democrats sweep Congress in a historic rebuke of Trump, Texas elects a Democratic governor, and Melania Trump hosts Ukraine and Russia

stories.title: Democrats win the House and the Senate, taking full control of Congress from Trump's Republicans
facts: AP called it overnight: Democrats won the House on top of the Senate, with voters frustrated over prices, the Iran war and corruption.
Democrats reached 218 House seats when Johnny Garcia won Texas's 35th District, a seat redrawn to favour Republicans, and they flipped districts Trump carried by up to 18 points.
In the Senate, Democrats took seats in Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina, per AP; Kansas hadn't elected a Democratic senator in 94 years.
Troy Jackson unseated Susan Collins in Maine, James Talarico beat Ken Paxton for Texas's Senate seat, Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted in Ohio and Roy Cooper flipped North Carolina.
The Washington Post calls it a historic rebuke not seen since 1974, and CBS exit polls put Trump's approval at 38%.
Hakeem Jeffries is expected to become Speaker, and Rep. Robert Garcia's message to the president was "LAWYER UP".
stories.whyItMatters: For Trump's last two years, every bill, budget and investigation now runs through a Democratic Congress.

stories.title: Texas gets its first Democratic governor in 35 years, and Missouri voters reject an abortion ban
facts: Democrat Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott in Texas, making her the state's first Democratic governor in 35 years and its first Hispanic governor.
In Ohio, Amy Acton is projected to beat Vivek Ramaswamy for governor.
Keisha Lance Bottoms beat Rick Jackson to become Georgia's next governor.
A Missouri ballot measure to ban abortion failed.
stories.whyItMatters: The wave reached state capitols in places Democrats hadn't won in decades, not just Congress.

image.alt: Amy Acton at a campaign event

stories.title: Trump says he'll accept the results and admits the Iran war was "a piece of" the defeat
facts: Trump told the New York Times he is "absolutely willing" to accept the results and expects to "work something out" with Democrats.
To the Wall Street Journal he said "Iran was a piece of it", blamed oil and gas prices more than the war itself, and said he'd do it again.
He told Fox News Democrats will send him "insane" bills that he'll veto until they come to the table.
On Truth Social he wrote that if he'd been on the ballot, Republicans would have won in a landslide.
stories.whyItMatters: With Congress gone, the Iran war and gas prices become the main fight for the rest of his term.

image.alt: Trump Acknowledges Iran War Is Partly to Blame for Republican Losses

stories.title: Melania Trump will host Ukrainian and Russian representatives at the White House on Thursday
facts: The first lady will speak about a local ceasefire in Russian-held Oleshky in the Kherson region on Thursday at 11:00 ET, which is 17:00 Berlin time.
The truce ran from October 27 to November 1 and allowed evacuations from the town.
RFE/RL's sources say Ukraine sends David Arakhamia and ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, and Russia sends Kirill Dmitriev and rights commissioner Yana Lantratova.
Lantratova has been under US sanctions since 2022.
A new round of US-mediated peace talks is set for next week.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the first time both sides will sit in the same room at the White House, even if the topic is one town.

stories.title: Better Auth patches 12 security holes, one critical, so update to 1.7.16 now
facts: Better Auth 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.5 fix 12 advisories.
The critical one (CVSS 9.1) is in @better-auth/expo. If you register the expo() plugin, rotate your app secret after upgrading.
A high-severity Electron plugin flaw could expose the server secret and skip two-factor, so rotate the auth secret and every social provider client secret.
Another high-severity bug let phone numbers be claimed before verification; medium ones hit MySQL serial-ID adapters and revoked sessions.
Vercel's WAF rules apply automatically, but it says they don't replace upgrading every better-auth and @better-auth/* package.
stories.whyItMatters: Better Auth is a common auth library in TypeScript apps, and several fixes need secret rotation, not just a version bump.

facts.text: Claude Code 2.1.317 loosens the Opus 5.5 rule that refused game projects: naming a game to describe mechanics now gets you an original game, and asking for a straight copy gets an offer to build something similar.
Vercel Security Review is in public beta, and Vercel CI no longer needs a linked Vercel project.
vercel doctor finds and fixes Vercel CLI setup issues without logging in or linking, with --json output for agents.
agent-browser now warns when your Chrome is outdated or behind on CVE fixes.
The Oxc team made Rolldown's bundling benchmarks another 3–6% faster, mostly from oxc-parser.
TypeScript merged a new --disableDynamicImportExtensionRewriting flag, and Bun removed another 315 unsafe blocks across two PRs.
